docs.text: Hi, I am Kai Wang. I am building my personal website while learning how to connect technology, design, and expression. This site records my course notes, projects, tool practice, and stage-by-stage reflections.

docs.title: Current Position
docs.text: I hope to gradually become someone who can explain problems clearly, make interfaces clear, and turn ideas into real work. This website is my long-term practice space.

docs.title: I Want This Site To Become
docs.text:
• A clear learning archive
  • A continuously updated portfolio
  • A personal space that reflects taste and judgment
  • A place where I can truly turn ideas into reality

docs.title: Website Building and Content Organization
docs.text: Learning how page structure, navigation, search, and long-term content maintenance connect.

docs.title: Product Display and Interaction Design
docs.text: Observing the hierarchy, rhythm, and feedback of strong websites, then translating them into my own design practice.

docs.title: AI-assisted Learning and Creation

docs.title: Long-term Personal Brand Building
docs.text: Letting projects, notes, and thoughts gradually form a stable, credible, and updateable personal entry point.

docs.title: Next Step
docs.text: I will continue improving the content structure of this site and gradually fill in courses, projects, and design observations. Instead of finishing everything at once, I hope it becomes a space that grows with me.

docs.title: Design as a way to make thinking easier to follow.
docs.text:
This page records the layer behind visual style: how I organize information, decide what matters, and shape a personal website into a working system rather than a collection of separate pages.

Information Structure Interaction Judgment Writing Iteration

docs.title: The page should feel designed, but the design should point back to the work.
docs.text:
Good personal sites are not only portfolios. They are learning records, project shelves, research notebooks, and small publishing systems. The visual layer matters because it helps people trust the structure underneath.

02

03

docs.title: Notice
docs.text: Capture useful moments from courses, projects, readings, and travel.

docs.title: Sort
docs.text: Place each piece of content in a clear category before styling it.

docs.title: Shape
docs.text: Choose layout, rhythm, and emphasis based on what the reader needs.

docs.title: Test
docs.text: Check whether the page is readable, usable, and consistent across languages.

docs.title: Iterate
docs.text: Keep refining details without losing the original structure.

docs.title: From isolated pages to a personal system.
docs.text: Each page should have a clear role. The homepage creates direction, course pages hold learning records, project pages show practice, blog pages keep experiences, and the About page explains the person behind the work.

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Help readers understand where they are and where to go next.

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text: Keep navigation, spacing, and page rhythm consistent across sections.

docs.title: Memory
docs.text: Let older notes remain findable as the site grows.

docs.title: Design decisions become easier when the page has a job.
docs.text: Instead of asking whether an element looks interesting, I want to ask whether it helps the page do its job: introduce a topic, compare ideas, show evidence, or invite the next action.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: The reader should always know the current section and have a simple way to move.

docs.title: Hierarchy
docs.text: Headings, tags, images, and notes should form a calm reading order.

docs.title: Interaction
docs.text: Motion and clickable modules should reveal information rather than distract.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text: The structure should still work after new courses, projects, and notes are added.

docs.title: Keep building a site that can hold both work and thought.
docs.text: The next step is to make every section feel connected: project details should explain process, blog pages should preserve lived experience, and the About area should make the whole site feel personal without becoming decorative.

Design Research Course

Course Notes (Gemini Notebook)

docs.title: Sample Note
docs.text:
This is a reusable course note template. When adding future articles, copy this structure and replace the text with your own content.

Course note Reusable template Work in progress

Writing goal: Make a course note more than a record. It should help readers understand the topic, see your judgment, and know what to do next.

docs.title: Topic
docs.text:
Describe the topic in one sentence and connect it to your long-term direction.

  • What problem does this note address?
  • How does it relate to interaction design, products, AI, or personal knowledge management?
  • What is the one idea readers should remember?

docs.title: Understand
docs.text: Explain the core concept in your own words instead of only copying source material.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text: Turn the idea into a small exercise, page, diagram, workflow, or reusable method.

docs.title: Reflect
docs.text: Record what you agree with, what you question, and where this knowledge may be useful.

docs.title: Extend
docs.text: Keep useful links, keywords, and follow-up questions for future research.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Material for MkDocs documentation
  • Notion-style content organization
  • Add course links, papers, videos, tools, or examples here.

docs.title: Set the context
docs.text: Explain why this topic matters and how it connects to your current project.

docs.title: Break down concepts
docs.text: Turn source material into 3 to 5 key concepts, each with a concise explanation.

docs.title: Make a small output
docs.text: Use a diagram, code snippet, prototype, or case example to test your understanding.

docs.title: Summarize
docs.text: Write three to five sentences about the takeaway, open questions, and next step.

docs.title: What if there is too much content?
docs.text: Keep the main thread first. Put details into references or follow-up questions so the page keeps a clear focus.

docs.title: What if I do not know how to summarize?
docs.text: Start with three prompts: what problem it solves, where you may use it, and what its limits are.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A good course note should feel like a refined knowledge card: clear topic, personal judgment, reading path, and useful references. The page does not need to be complex, but every module should have a clear reading purpose.

docs.text:
2026.02-03

Core Question

78.6% Young children spend more than 1 hour on screens each day

53.0% Young children spend more than 2 hours on screens each day

3 Dimensions Language interaction, physical participation, and emotional response form high-quality parent-child interaction

01 / Problem Finding

Improvisational storytelling games show strong interaction potential across language, body, and emotion.

02 / User Insight

In the user journey, the emotional curve drops clearly during the storytelling stagnation stage, making it the key moment for system support.

03 / Design Opportunities

04 / System Plan

The system assistance level changes with the narrative state: it steps back when the story is smooth, intervenes lightly when the story gets stuck, and helps organize after the session ends.

05 / Hardware Design

The exploration ring supports observation, action, and help-seeking, connecting story progression with body movement.

06 / Software Design

The interface uses a lightweight and child-friendly visual language to organize exploration entry points, prop status, and story outcomes.

07 / Prototype Validation

Project Reflection

Back to Projects

docs.title: COSTORY
docs.text: COSTORY uses a physical prop and AI-assisted guidance to provide plot prompts and feedback, helping parents and children co-create stories through higher-quality interaction.   3 Weeks Individual Work Product Design Interaction Design AI Prototype

docs.title: Project Motivation
docs.text: BEGIN

docs.title: How can we reduce the risk of storytelling breakdown without interrupting parent-child co-creation?
docs.text: COSTORY does not use AI to tell stories for children. Instead, when parent-child interaction weakens, the story gets stuck, or the next direction becomes unclear, it provides lightweight prompts, scene feedback, and story organization. The system aims to shift the screen from a controller into an assistant, bringing physical participation, language expression, and emotional response back to the center of parent-child interaction.

docs.title: The screen is not the only problem. Interaction quality matters more.
docs.text: Young children's screen exposure is commonly high, but the design opportunity is not simply to tell them to use screens less. The more meaningful question is how to bring attention back to shared parent-child activity. After research, I focused on improvisational storytelling games because they naturally combine language expression, physical participation, and emotional response.

docs.title: The moment of getting stuck is where co-creation breaks most easily.
docs.text: Parents are willing to participate, but they often lack a stable way to guide the story. Children are used to screen content pushing the experience forward, and once free expression meets a blank moment, they can easily lose interest. The design goal therefore shifted from providing more content to providing the right direction at the point of stagnation.

docs.title: Three design opportunities: scene, guidance, and direction.
Immersive Scene
docs.text: Turn abstract text into observable and imaginable visuals so children can quickly enter the story.

docs.title: AI-assisted Guidance
docs.text: When the story gets stuck, provide fuzzy directions and inspiring prompts without making decisions for the users.

docs.title: Narrative Direction
docs.text: Break the story into characters, context, and events so parents and children can continue around clearer clues.

docs.title: From free co-creation to light AI intervention.
Context Introduction
docs.text: Users choose the narrative scene and characters, while the system provides an initial story framework.

docs.title: Free Progression
docs.text: Children and parents perform, narrate, and use the prop while the system records without interrupting.

docs.title: Stagnation Detection
docs.text: The system judges whether intervention is needed based on speech pauses, repeated actions, or active help requests.

docs.title: Structure Organization
docs.text: Fragmented expression is organized into story blocks: beginning, conflict, climax, and ending.

docs.title: Story Generation
docs.text: The system generates a complete story while preserving room for users to adjust structure and style.

docs.title: The exploration ring brings children back from the screen into physical interaction.
docs.text: The hardware prototype was developed from children's common play actions: observing, confronting, and exploring. It became a directional exploration ring. The IMU sensor recognizes waving, rotating, and lifting actions, while the vibration motor provides subtle reminders when the story gets stuck. This allows AI assistance to enter the interaction through touch instead of taking over screen attention.

docs.title: The software saves the story instead of replacing the live interaction.
docs.text: The software includes a welcome page, home page, prop page, story page, story viewer, and personal page. The core idea is not to keep children looking at the screen. Instead, the screen becomes an entry point, recording tool, and review space, while the actual story generation still comes from live language, actions, and shared parent-child imagination.

docs.title: Character Consistency
docs.text: Milo and Bubble Detective create stable recognition, making story changes across different scenes easier for children to understand.

docs.title: Context Introduction
docs.text: Open-ended questions and scene images guide children to express themselves without limiting imagination through fixed choices at the start.

docs.title: Light AI Prompts
docs.text: The system provides multiple development directions and fuzzy plot hints to help the story continue while preserving user choice.

docs.title: Story Organization
docs.text: Fragmented expression is organized into a staged narrative structure, while users can still adjust the narrative style.

docs.title: The key validation is not whether AI can generate, but whether the assistance stays restrained.
docs.text: Prototype validation focused on three levels: whether the hardware could recognize meaningful actions, whether AI could generate open prompts without replacing the users, and whether the final story could form a clear structure while preserving room for user editing. This direction helped narrow the project from an "AI storytelling tool" into a "parent-child co-creation support system."

docs.title: Action Recognition
docs.text: Acceleration and angular velocity are used to recognize waving, rotating, and lifting, providing action clues for story progression.

docs.title: Scene Generation
docs.text: Locations and change events are combined to generate scenes so that image and text semantics remain consistent.

docs.title: Development Direction
docs.text: AI generates directions around character, scene, and event instead of giving a complete answer directly.

docs.title: Complete Story
docs.text: The final story is generated from speech and action records while preserving structured editing space.

docs.title: The most important judgments I made in this project
Not adding more screen time, but changing the role of the screen
docs.text: The screen only supports entry, prompts, and review instead of becoming the center of parent-child interaction.

docs.title: AI should not complete imagination for the users
docs.text: Good AI intervention should feel like a gentle push, not a takeover of the story.

docs.title: Physical props make interaction more suitable for children
docs.text: The exploration ring connects seeing and moving, so story progression does not depend only on language and tapping.

docs.title: Personal Website System
docs.text:
2026-08-present Personal Portfolio

A personal portfolio website that is continuously built and iterated.

A personal portfolio website that is continuously built and iterated.

GitHub Repository

As a non-technical student, it is hard for me to build a personal site from bottom to the end, which is also a good chance for me to take this attemptation.

GOAL 01

Turn the portfolio into a system, not a one-off page.

The site needs to hold the homepage, course notes, project cases, links, and about information while staying clear as more content is added in the future.

GOAL 02

Make content maintenance possible for low-code users.

The website manager brings page selection, content editing, module insertion, preview, build, and deployment into one place, reducing the pressure of editing code directly.

GOAL 03

Give AI collaboration clear judgment criteria.

Each iteration is not only about making the page look better. It also checks whether the positioning is clear, projects are readable, interactions are necessary, and Chinese and English pages stay aligned.

docs.title: Personal Website Design
docs.text: WEBSITE SYSTEM

docs.title: Why Design a Personal Website
docs.text: WHY

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• Build a stable information structure with MkDocs and Material
  • Add personal visual style and interaction through custom CSS and JavaScript
  • Maintain bilingual content with Chinese and English directories
  • Use a local manager to lower the daily editing threshold
  • Publish the site through GitHub Pages

docs.title: Homepage Project Entry
docs.text: The homepage uses a large headline, stacked project cards, and drag-to-switch interaction so visitors can see representative work immediately.

docs.title: Modular Content
docs.text: The course, project, links, and about pages use richer modules instead of plain Markdown paragraphs only.

docs.title: Maintainable Features
docs.text: Search, bilingual switching, light / dark / system color mode, and GitHub Pages publishing have been added.

docs.title: Website Manager
docs.text: The manager provides page selection, new page creation, module insertion, preview, build, and deployment actions as the basis for future low-code maintenance.

docs.title: Next Direction
docs.text: Next focus: Move the manager from code-editing assistance toward visual content editing, so common modules can be added, edited, and reordered like cards.

docs.title: 示例课程文档
docs.text:
这是一篇示例课程文档。以后新增文章时，可以复制这个结构，再替换成自己的内容。

课程笔记 可复用模板 更新中

写作目标： 让一篇课程笔记不只是“记录内容”，而是能帮助读者快速理解主题、看到你的判断，并找到后续行动。

docs.title: 课程主题
docs.text:
用一句话说明这篇文章在讲什么，并把它和你的长期方向联系起来。

  • 这篇文章解决什么问题？
  • 它和交互设计、产品、AI 或个人知识管理有什么关系？
  • 读完以后，读者应该记住哪一个核心观点？

docs.title: 理解概念
docs.text: 用自己的话解释核心概念，不只是复制资料。好的笔记应该能体现你是否真的理解了这个主题。

docs.title: 完成练习
docs.text: 把知识转化成一个小练习、一个页面、一个流程图，或者一段可以被复用的方法。

docs.title: 记录判断
docs.text: 写下你认同什么、不认同什么，以及这个知识未来可能用在哪里。

docs.title: 留下入口
docs.text: 保存参考链接、关键词和延伸问题，方便以后继续深入。

docs.title: 参考资料
docs.text:
• Material for MkDocs 文档
  • Notion 风格内容组织参考
  • 这里可以继续放课程链接、论文、视频、工具或案例。

docs.title: 准备背景
docs.text: 先写清楚为什么学这个主题，以及它和你当前项目之间的关系。

docs.title: 拆出概念
docs.text: 把大段资料拆成 3 到 5 个关键概念，每个概念只保留最重要的解释。

docs.title: 做一个小练习
docs.text: 用图、表、代码、原型或案例验证自己是否真的理解。

docs.title: 写下总结
docs.text: 用三到五句话说明收获、问题和下一步。

docs.title: 内容太多怎么办？
docs.text: 先保留主线。细节可以放到“参考资料”或“延伸问题”，不要让页面失去重点。

docs.title: 不知道怎么总结怎么办？
docs.text: 可以从“这个知识解决了什么问题”“我会在哪里用它”“它有什么限制”三个角度写。

docs.title: 总结
docs.text: 一篇好的课程文档，应该像一张整理过的知识卡片：有主题、有判断、有路径，也有可以继续追踪的资料。页面不用复杂，但每个模块都要承担清晰的阅读任务。

docs.title: COSTORY
docs.text:
亲子即兴故事共创

核心命题

78.6% 低龄儿童每日屏幕时间超过 1 小时

53.0% 低龄儿童每日屏幕时间超过 2 小时

3 个维度 语言互动、身体参与、情感回应共同构成高质量亲子互动

01 / 问题发现

即兴故事游戏在语言、身体和情感三个维度上都具备较高互动潜力。

02 / 用户洞察

用户旅程中，游戏停滞阶段的情绪曲线明显下降，是最需要系统辅助的节点。

03 / 设计机会

04 / 系统方案

系统辅助强度随叙事状态变化：顺畅时退后，卡住时轻介入，结束后帮助整理。

05 / 硬件设计

探索环承担观察、行动和求助三个角色，让故事推进和身体动作产生连接。

06 / 软件设计

界面采用轻量、童趣的视觉语言，把探索入口、道具状态和故事成果组织在一起。

07 / 原型验证

docs.title: COSTORY
docs.text: 借助实体道具与 AI 辅助提供情节引导与反馈，让亲子在高质量互动中共创故事。   3 Weeks 个人作品 产品设计 交互设计 AI 原型

docs.title: 项目初心
docs.text: BEGIN

docs.title: 如何在不打断亲子共创的前提下，降低即兴叙事的停滞风险？
docs.text: COSTORY 不是用 AI 直接替孩子讲故事，而是在孩子和家长的互动变弱、叙事卡住或缺少方向时，提供轻量提示、场景反馈和故事整理。系统希望把屏幕从“主导者”变成“辅助者”，让身体参与、语言表达和情感回应重新成为亲子互动的中心。

docs.title: 屏幕不是唯一问题，互动质量才是关键。
docs.text: 低龄儿童的屏幕暴露时间普遍偏高，但真正值得设计介入的不是简单“少看屏幕”，而是如何把注意力重新带回到亲子共同活动里。调研后我把机会落在“即兴故事游戏”上，因为它同时需要语言表达、身体参与和情绪回应。

docs.title: 卡住的瞬间，是亲子共创最容易断掉的地方。
docs.text: 家长愿意参与互动，但缺少稳定的故事引导方式；孩子习惯被屏幕内容推进，一旦自由表达遇到空白，就容易失去兴趣。于是设计目标从“提供更多内容”转向“在停滞点提供恰到好处的方向”。

docs.title: 三个设计机会：场景、引导、方向。
沉浸场景
docs.text: 把抽象文本变成可观察、可想象的具体画面，帮助孩子快速进入故事。

docs.title: AI 辅助引导
docs.text: 当叙事停滞时，只给模糊方向和启发式提示，不替用户做决定。

docs.title: 叙事方向
docs.text: 把故事拆成角色、情境、事件，让亲子可以围绕清晰线索继续推进。

docs.title: 从自由共创到 AI 轻介入。
情境引入
docs.text: 用户选择叙事场景与角色，系统提供初始情境框架。

docs.title: 自由推进
docs.text: 孩子和家长表演、叙述、使用道具，系统只记录不打断。

docs.title: 卡住识别
docs.text: 根据语言停顿、动作重复或主动求助，判断是否需要介入。

docs.title: 结构整理
docs.text: 把碎片表达整理成“开始-冲突-高潮-结局”的故事块。

docs.title: 故事生成
docs.text: 生成完整故事，同时保留用户对结构和风格的修改空间。

docs.title: 用“探索环”把孩子从屏幕前拉回身体互动。
docs.text: 硬件原型从儿童游戏中常见的观察、对抗和探索动作出发，形成一个带有方向感的探索环。IMU 传感器识别挥动、旋转和举起动作，震动马达在故事卡住时给出轻提示，让 AI 辅助以触觉方式进入互动，而不是抢占屏幕注意力。

docs.title: 软件界面负责保存故事，而不是替代现场互动。
docs.text: 软件端包含欢迎页、首页、道具页、故事页、查看故事和个人页。核心设计不是让孩子一直看屏幕，而是把屏幕变成故事入口、记录工具和回顾空间；真正的故事生成仍然来自现场语言、动作和亲子共同想象。

docs.title: 角色一致性
docs.text: 通过 Milo 与泡泡侦探两个角色建立稳定识别，让不同场景中的故事变化更容易被孩子理解。

docs.title: 情境引入
docs.text: 用开放式问题与场景图引导孩子表达，避免一开始就用固定选项限制想象。

docs.title: AI 轻提示
docs.text: 系统提供多条发展方向和模糊情节提示，帮助继续故事，但保留用户选择权。

docs.title: 故事整理
docs.text: 将碎片表达整理为阶段化叙事结构，同时支持用户调整叙事风格。

docs.title: 验证重点不是“能不能生成”，而是“辅助是否克制”。
docs.text: 原型验证分成三个层面：硬件能否识别有效动作；AI 是否能生成开放但不替代用户的提示；最终故事是否能在保留用户修改空间的前提下形成清晰结构。这个验证方向也帮助我把项目从“AI 讲故事工具”收束为“亲子共创辅助系统”。

docs.title: 动作识别
docs.text: 基于加速度与角速度识别挥动、旋转和举起，为故事推进提供动作线索。

docs.title: 场景生成
docs.text: 用地点和变化事件组合生成场景，让图像和文本语义保持一致。

docs.title: 发展方向
docs.text: AI 生成“角色-场景-事件”方向，不直接给完整答案。

docs.title: 完整故事
docs.text: 根据语音记录与动作记录生成完整故事，并保留结构化修改空间。

docs.title: 我在这个项目中最重要的判断
不是增加屏幕，而是改变屏幕角色
docs.text: 屏幕只承担入口、提示和回顾，不成为亲子互动的中心。

docs.title: AI 不应该替用户完成想象
docs.text: 好的 AI 介入应该像一个轻轻推一下的同伴，而不是直接接管故事。

docs.title: 实体道具让交互更适合儿童
docs.text: 探索环把“看”和“动”联系起来，让故事推进不只依赖语言和点击。

docs.title: 个人网站系统
docs.text:
2026.08-至今 个人 作品集

一个持续搭建和迭代的个人作品集网页。

一个持续搭建和迭代的个人作品集网页。

GitHub 项目仓库

GOAL 01

让作品集变成系统，而不是一次性页面。

网站需要同时承载首页、课程笔记、项目案例、友链和关于信息，并在未来内容增加后仍然保持清晰结构。

GOAL 02

让低代码用户也能维护内容。

通过网站管理器把页面选择、内容编辑、模块插入、预览、构建和部署流程集中起来，减少直接修改代码的压力。

GOAL 03

让 AI 协作有清晰判断标准。

每次修改不只追求“看起来好看”，还要检查定位是否清楚、项目是否可读、交互是否必要、中英文是否一致。

docs.title: 个人网站设计
docs.text: WEBSITE SYSTEM

docs.title: 为什么要设计个人网页
docs.text: WHY

docs.title: 方法
docs.text:
• 用 MkDocs 和 Material 搭建稳定的信息结构
  • 用自定义 CSS 和 JavaScript 补充个人化视觉与交互
  • 用中英文目录维护双语内容
  • 用本地管理器降低日常编辑门槛
  • 用 GitHub Pages 完成公开托管

docs.title: 首页作品入口
docs.text: 首页用大标题、项目卡片堆叠和拖拽切换，让访客一进来就能看到代表作品。

docs.title: 内容模块化
docs.text: 课程、项目、友链和关于页面都采用更丰富的模块，而不是只有普通 Markdown 段落。

docs.title: 可维护功能
docs.text: 已经加入搜索、中英文切换、浅色 / 深色 / 跟随系统主题，以及 GitHub Pages 发布流程。

docs.title: 网站管理器
docs.text: 管理器提供页面选择、新建页面、模块插入、预览、构建和部署入口，是后续低代码维护的基础。

docs.title: 后续修改方向
docs.text: 下一步重点： 把管理器从“代码编辑辅助”继续推进到“可视化内容编辑”，让常用模块可以像卡片一样被新增、修改和重排。
